old_memory_protocol.description: Retroactively assigned label and hash; no formal protocol or contract hash existed at the time these files were produced. ME construction was: one MemoryItem per session, built by concatenating every seeker dialogue turn in that session into a single unbounded-length string. builder_contract_sha256_retroactive is sha256(canonical_json(descriptor)) above, independently reproducible from the descriptor field.

new_memory_protocol.description: build_evo_memory's ME construction now chunks each session's seeker turns into non-overlapping, in-order, length-bounded episode items with stable turn-span ids (60-token reporting target, 120-token true hard cap -- any turn alone over the cap is losslessly split on sentence/word/bounded-character-span boundaries into further uniquely-id'd sub-spans), instead of one whole-session item.

reason: This is a checked-in snapshot of scripts/15b_evoemo_pm_readiness.py's output (pm_action_distribution, safe_action_count_distribution, etc.), derived from make_evo_runtime_state()/_catalog() statistics over build_evo_memory()'s items. The chunked ME catalog changes count/age/token features that gate the PM's OOD/safe-action logic, so a fresh run under the current builder would very plausibly produce different distributions. No script or test regenerates or diffs it against a live run, so it would otherwise go silently stale.

action_if_regenerated: Any regeneration under the current or a future builder must be written to a NEW path, never overwritten in place here. A formal V1.5 consumer that encounters builder_contract_sha256 == "9ec603028cceb522d1f3da7062962e6cdd3ed9d2d23dfca65d0d5a7dafecd964" (the old, retroactively-labeled contract) must fail closed rather than treat the file as current.
